texts.R1: F1 (entry into force). For every issue act a with f(a) = t ∈ T: σ(t)(τ(a)) = v(a). It says nothing about σ at other times, and nothing about acts with f(a) = ∞
texts.R6: Work-event attribute typing. Every work event has τ(w) ∈ 𝒯, α(w) ∈ 𝒜, t(w) ∈ T
texts.R9: Reference and constitution typing. Ref ⊆ R × (E ∪ W); con : E ⇀ R is partial (may be undefined everywhere). If (ρ, a) ∈ Ref and con(a) ≠ ρ, then ρ reports a (definitional)
texts.R11: Norm state is a total primitive, not computed from acts. σ : T → V^𝒯 is total; no frame axiom derives σ from E. σ is constrained only through F1 (A5): F1 does fix σ(f(a))(τ(a)) = v(a) at every finite entry into force (R1), but nothing determines σ elsewhere from acts
texts.R14: No equation between f and d or r ("f ≠ r/d" in the sense *no equation*): the frame never equates entry into force with recording or decision time. It equally imposes no inequality: f may coincide with d or r in some histories
texts.R15: No time order among r, d, f beyond F2; t(w) outside the governance times. The frame imposes no order between r, d and f except d = r under constitution (R3), and treats t(w) as a work attribute, not a governance time
texts.R16: No completeness constraint. The frame does not require that every act or work event is referenced by some record; absence is NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE, not non-occurrence
texts.R17: No norm→work dependence. The frame does not require that a norm value implies or excludes any act or work event
texts.R21: Texts are texts. No axiom ties the text c to σ or f (A5): a self-assertion such as "effective immediately" or "remains blocked" is a value of c, not an observation of σ or f. (Σ and V are not declared disjoint by Def 1.1; the point is the absence of a tie, not a type distinction)
texts.R79: B-side record clause replaced by "E ≠ ∅" (R-i): H-B requires only that some act exists, not that a record references it
texts.R80: No B-side record clause (R-i′): H-B carries no record requirement; "acts exist" is read as a joint statement about both hypotheses

concepts: Participant (an actor, i.e. an identity that items refer to; what it is *able* to do is C2, not part of this row)
Capability of a participant for an act kind (issue / adopt), constant within a history
Governed target (the subject a norm is about, e.g. a work package)
Deontic value, with a distinguished subset of values that permit work to begin
Norm as a pair (target, value) only
Norm state (value in force per target per time), held as its own primitive, not computed from acts
Change point of the norm state (target, time at which the value differs)
Issue act (participant, norm, prepared flag). Its decision time is in C11 and its entry into force in C12, both unobserved, so neither is part of this row
Adoption act whose object is an issue act
Prepared / adopted status of an issue act (derived: prepared flag plus capable adoption by a time)
Entry into force of an issue act (a time, or never)
Record (identity, recording time, text). The keeper is unobserved in general and belongs to C16, not this row
Recording time of a record (as reported; possibly missing)
Record text as text, including self-asserted statements of force or status ("effective immediately", "remains blocked") held as content
Reference from a record to an act or work event ("carries or references")
Report-vs-constitution mode of a record–act pair, held as *unknown-capable* (record reports the act / record is the act / undetermined)
Work event (target, executor). Its start time is unobserved and belongs to C20, not this row
Conformance / violation of a work event against the norm state at its start
Three governance times kept distinct (recording, decision, entry into force), with the work start time outside them
Not-evidenced-in-capture (an act or work event no record references; capture incompleteness)
Execution trace (a capture item ordered by recording order only)
Record independence for a target (keeper is neither norm-maker nor executor; record constitutes no act on that target)
Norm-state attestation channel (an external observable reporting the norm state for a work event's target at its start time)
Mode-undetermined flag on a record–act pair (performative ambiguity as a property of what is observable, not of one history)
Two independent limitation kinds on any norm-state claim: structural non-identifiability vs instrument unreliability
